title: Entity-level co-change (function granularity)
description:
Lift sutra_cochange from file-level to function-level granularity. Currently sutra computes co-change as file-level Jaccard similarity over the git commit×file matrix within a 90-day window. This is useful but coarse — "these two files change together" is less actionable than "these two functions change together."

sem's approach: walks git history once (bounded by max_commits), intersects commit diffs with entity line ranges to get per-commit entity change sets, then computes both hotspot churn counts and co-change pairs simultaneously. `CoChangePair { a_name, a_file, b_name, b_file, together, a_commits, b_commits, confidence }` where `confidence = together / min(a_commits, b_commits)`. Caps commits with too many entity changes (`MAX_PAIR_ENTITIES`) to avoid combinatorial blowup on giant refactors.

Key design consideration: sem also has an `entity_changes` table in its MCP cache (persisted commit→entity index: commit_sha, entity_name/type/file, change_type, old_name/path, structural flag). This avoids re-walking git on every query. Sutra should consider a similar persistent index — the git walk + line-range intersection is the expensive part.

Reference implementation:
- `sutra-surveys/sem/crates/sem-core/src/parser/hotspot.rs` — `CoChangePair`, `compute_history_analytics()`, `aggregate_history_analytics()`, `MAX_PAIR_ENTITIES`
- `sutra-surveys/sem/crates/sem-mcp/src/cache.rs` — `entity_changes` table schema

Sutra integration points:
- `sutra/src/tools/cochange.rs` — current file-level implementation
- `sutra/src/tools/trend.rs` — existing git history walking
- `sutra/src/health/ondemand.rs` — FunctionHotspot biomarker already intersects git blame lines with symbol ranges (similar technique, different purpose)

License: MIT → AGPL fine with attribution.

decisions.decision: Per-commit blob re-parse via symbol_diff (sem's model) over blame-based intersection
decisions.rationale: Blame maps only current-HEAD lines — structurally blind to deleted/renamed entities and limited to changed-paths call sites; symbol_diff gives historically-accurate ranges per commit and is nearly free to reuse after 226/227
decisions.rejected: FunctionHotspot-style git-blame × current symbol ranges — cheaper per query but wrong tool for a persistent history index

decisions.decision: Incremental sha-keyed append-only store, separate tables from commit_files
decisions.rationale: commit_files is wholesale-wiped every index run; entity walk is too expensive to redo and history should accumulate past any window; sha-keying makes it branch-agnostic with no invalidation story needed
decisions.rejected: Extending commit_files / the 90-day wipe-and-rebuild model — repeated reparse cost and permanent history loss

decisions.decision: Report both jaccard and confidence per pair
decisions.rationale: They answer different questions (symmetric coupling strength vs 'the rarer entity never moves alone'); both are cheap from the same counts
decisions.rejected: Picking one metric — sem's confidence-only loses comparability with sutra's existing file-level jaccard output

implementation_plan:
Design settled 2026-07-10. Corrections to original description: trend.rs is the WRONG pointer — it diffs health snapshots, no git walking. Real precedents: git.rs/pipeline.rs file-level commit walk (commit_files, wholesale-rebuilt every index over a rolling 90-day window via replace_commit_files, graph.rs:73-97) and health/ondemand.rs FunctionHotspot (blame × current-HEAD ranges — cheap but blind to deleted/renamed entities and changed-paths-only).

Core move: reuse symbol_diff as the per-commit entity differ. diff_file already re-parses two git blobs and classifies per symbol — exactly sem's compute_semantic_diff. After sutra/227 it also tracks renames, so co-change chains survive renames (better than sem).

Plan (depends on sutra/227):
1. Migration: new tables entity_commits(hash PK, committed_at, author) + entity_changes(commit_hash, qualified_name, kind, file_path, change_type, old_qualified_name, old_file_path, pair_eligible), indexed on commit_hash and qualified_name. MUST be separate from commits/commit_files — those are wiped every index run by replace_commit_files; these are append-only and sha-keyed (branch-agnostic, immutable, never re-diffed).
2. Index-time incremental walk (pipeline post-index step): git rev-list --first-parent bounded by max_commits (default 500 for initial backfill; steady state only new shas). Skip shas already in entity_commits. Per new commit: changed files vs first parent, run symbol_diff::diff_file per file (reusing 226/227 machinery — renames land as change_type=renamed with old_qualified_name), insert rows. Merge commits → row in entity_commits, zero entity_changes (first-parent diffs of individual commits already cover the content, per sem cache.rs:301-309).
3. Guards ported from sem hotspot.rs: dedup entity keys per commit; if a commit touches > MAX_PAIR_ENTITIES=50 entities, mark its rows pair_eligible=false (skipped for pair-counting, still counted for churn) — kills quadratic blowup on bulk refactors. Log/store a pair_commits_skipped count.
4. Query side: cochange.rs gains granularity: file|function param (default file, existing behavior untouched). Function-level aggregation over entity_changes: pair counts per commit (pair_eligible only), filter together >= 2, report BOTH metrics per pair: jaccard = together/(a+b-together) AND confidence = together/min(a,b) (sem hotspot.rs:252). Threshold param applies to jaccard for consistency with the file-level tool.
5. Rename continuity: when aggregating, chase old_qualified_name → qualified_name renames so a renamed function's history counts as one entity (single-hop is enough; multi-hop chains are rare and can be iterative).

Tests: two functions co-edited across 3 commits → pair with correct together/confidence/jaccard; bulk commit >50 entities → excluded from pairs, present in churn; renamed function keeps accumulating with its pre-rename identity; merge commits contribute no rows; re-run of walk is a no-op for seen shas.
execution_record:
Implementation followed the plan closely. Two commits on main:

1. `78c78e2` — Core implementation: migration 0048 (entity_commits + entity_changes tables, Durable partition), git history walking (git_first_parent_commits with merge detection, git_commit_changed_files), DB layer (insert_entity_commit_with_changes with MAX_PAIR_ENTITIES=50 guard, entity_cochange_for_symbol with rename continuity via old_qualified_name chasing, both jaccard and confidence metrics), pipeline integration (entity_change_walk in post_parse_sequence after commit_files), cochange tool update (granularity param: file|function).

2. `a8a810e` — Tests + idempotent insert guard: 8 entity-level tests (two-function co-edit, bulk commit exclusion, rename continuity, merge commits, idempotent insert, min-shared filter, known_hashes). Fixed insert_entity_commit_with_changes to skip entity_changes when commit hash already exists.

Live validation on sutra itself: 499 commits indexed, 9549 entity changes, 44 commits pair_ineligible (>50 entities). Initial backfill completed within the normal 15s parse window. Steady-state overhead: zero (all SHAs already known).

No divergence from plan. symbol_diff::diff_file reuse worked exactly as designed — renames land with old_qualified_name populated from 227 work.

messages.text:
Codex adversarial review (3 findings):

1. [high] Partial indexing failures recorded as successful commits — FIXED in 7143532. git_commit_changed_files failures now skip instead of inserting empty entity_commits rows.

2. [high] Root commits miss entity changes (git diff-tree without --root) — FIXED in 7143532. Added --root flag.

3. [medium] Rename continuity only follows one hop — BY DESIGN per implementation plan: "single-hop is enough; multi-hop chains are rare and can be iterative." Not a bug.

edges.note: entity_changes rows reuse symbol_diff incl. rename-aware change_type
